title: Jensen Huang at Stanford GSB: creating markets, first principles, flat orgs, core beliefs
summary: Jensen recounts founding NVIDIA, the OpenGL pivot that saved it, and creating markets alongside technology. He explains first-principles thinking, early indicators of future success, his flat organization with about 50 direct reports, and how he steadied the company through an 80% stock drop.

principles.text: Create the market while you create the technology; for new computing the two can't be separated.
principles.quote: we had to create technology, create markets. The idea that a company would create technology, create markets, defines NVIDIA today.

principles.text: Treat unfamiliar problems as learnable, then rebuild from first principles instead of copying.
principles.quote: my first thought is always, how hard can it be? And it's probably just a textbook away. You're probably one archive paper away from figuring this out.

principles.text: Use early indicators of future success, not lagging results, to keep conviction in far-off bets.
principles.quote: gross margins. That's not a KPI, that's a result. You're looking for something that's an early indicators of future positive result

principles.text: Choose work by its importance and whether it would happen without you, not by market size.
principles.quote: We find inspiration not from the size of a market, but from the importance of the work.

principles.text: In a crisis, gut-check your core beliefs; change nothing unless the underlying facts changed.
principles.quote: if those things change, you've gotta change everything. But if none of those things change, you change nothing, keep on going

principles.text: Design the organization from first principles and let information flow freely rather than hoarding it.
principles.quote: I don't believe in a culture, an environment, where the information that you possess is the reason why you have power.
